EventPageResponse.description:
A replay page.

``next_seq`` is the cursor to send on the following request, and ``has_more`` says
whether one is needed. Returning both means the client never has to infer whether a
short page meant "caught up" or "hit the limit".

EventResponse.description:
One event, as delivered over REST replay and over the socket.

The same shape on both paths on purpose: a client that can render a replayed event
can render a live one with no branching, which is what makes reconnection seamless.

JobStatus.description:
Where a job is in its lifecycle.

``FAILED`` is retryable — the job goes back to ``PENDING`` with backoff. ``DEAD`` is
terminal: attempts are exhausted and a human needs to look. Keeping them distinct is
what makes the dead-letter query "everything that gave up" rather than "everything
that ever failed".

info.description:
Control-plane API for the AI Software Factory.

Every error response uses a single envelope with a stable `error.code`; branch on that
rather than on status text. Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header that
correlates it with server logs.
info.title: AI Software Factory API

post.description:
Exchange a refresh token for a new session.

The presented token is consumed: a successor is issued and the old one is retired.
Presenting a retired token is treated as theft and revokes the whole session family.

Create an unverified account and email a one-time code.

202 rather than 201: the account exists but is not yet usable, and the meaningful work
— proving the address — has not finished.

The daily cap is not applied to this first code. The user has not asked for anything
yet, so refusing their very first code would be nonsensical.
post.summary: Create an account and send a verification code

post.description:
Issue a new code, superseding any previous one.

Answers identically for an unknown address and an already-verified one. Anything else
would turn this unauthenticated endpoint into an account-existence oracle. Rate limits
still apply to real accounts, so it cannot be used to flood an inbox.

Exchange credentials for a session.

An unknown email and a wrong password produce the same error, after the same amount of
work, so this endpoint cannot be used to discover which addresses are registered.

Correct credentials on an unverified account return ``email_not_verified`` (403). That
only ever reaches someone who already knows the password, so it is not an enumeration
vector — and the caller needs to know to go and enter their code.

Revoke a refresh token.

Idempotent, and deliberately indistinguishable for a token that never existed:
reporting the difference would tell an unauthenticated caller whether a token is real.

Redeem a code and start a session.

An unknown address produces the same error as a wrong code, so this endpoint cannot be
used to discover which addresses are registered. Redeeming a code proves ownership of
the address, so a session is issued without re-checking the password.

get.summary: Read the last verification code sent to an address (dev/test only)

get.description:
Report that this process is running.

Touches nothing external. A failure here means the process itself is broken and
should be restarted — which is exactly why it must not probe the database. An
orchestrator that restarts pods because Postgres blipped turns a brief database
problem into a full outage.

get.description:
Report every requirement and whether it is satisfied.

Satisfaction for a secret-backed requirement is derived from whether the secret
exists, so this cannot claim a credential is present when it is not.
get.summary: What this project still needs before it can be built

post.description:
Add a catalog requirement to this project.

Raises:
    ValidationError: The key is not in the catalog. Rejected here rather than ignored
        because a human typing a key deserves to be told; the intake agent in Phase 3
        uses the service directly, which drops unknown keys instead.
post.summary: Record that this project needs a configuration entry

post.description:
Create a run to carry events and jobs.

Phase 3's graph will own run creation. It is exposed now because events and jobs
both hang off a run, and the realtime pipeline has to be demonstrable before any
agent exists to drive it.

get.description:
Return every secret's metadata.

Names, descriptions and timestamps. Never values — there is no endpoint that returns
one, and no response model with a field for one.

delete.description:
Remove a secret.

Raises:
    NotFoundError: No secret by that name, so nothing was deleted. Reported rather
        than silently succeeding, because "delete succeeded" on a typo'd name would
        leave an operator believing a credential was revoked when it was not.

get.description:
Return one secret's metadata.

Raises:
    NotFoundError: No secret by that name in this project.

put.description:
Encrypt and store a value.

Idempotent by name: storing again replaces the value and bumps its version, so an
operator rotating a credential does not have to delete first.

Raises:
    ValidationError: The path name and body name disagree. Guessing which one was
        meant would silently write to the wrong key.
put.summary: Store or replace a secret value

post.description:
Return an archived project to ``draft``, making it writable again.

The counterpart to archiving. Without it, archiving is indistinguishable from a slow
delete, and users avoid it — which defeats the point of having it.
post.summary: Take a project out of the archive

get.description:
Report whether this process can serve traffic.

Returns 503 with a per-dependency breakdown when something it depends on is down, so
the load balancer stops routing here while the process stays up.

Return the events a client has not seen.

This is what makes a dropped socket lossless: the client sends the last ``seq`` it
processed and receives exactly the gap, in order, once.

Raises:
    NotFoundError: The run does not exist, or belongs to another user's project.

post.description:
Submit a job.

Enqueued in the request's own transaction, so the job and the state that justifies it
commit together — there is no window where a worker could claim a job referring to
something that was rolled back.
post.summary: Enqueue background work against a run

post.description:
Issue a short-lived ticket authorising one socket connection.

A ticket rather than a cookie (CSRF-prone on WebSocket) or a query-string bearer
token (which lands in access logs). See ``ws/tickets.py``.
post.summary: Mint a single-use ticket for the event socket
